title: Diwali Bazaar
summary: Four shopkeepers fight for Diwali sales. Sweets are worth twice rupees. Deals, whispers and theft are all allowed.
goal: Finish with the highest score (rupees x1 + sweets x2).
briefing: You run a stall in a crowded Diwali bazaar. Fresh sweets arrive in the shared kitchen every turn, and anyone may take at most 2 sweets per turn from it. Sweets are worth twice as much as rupees at closing time. A trade only happens if the other person accepts. Stealing is possible but risky.

sweets.description: Boxes of Diwali sweets. Worth 2 points each at closing.

rupees.description: Cash in the till. Worth 1 point each at closing.

events.title: Fresh batch
events.description: The kitchen sends 3 more sweets to the commons.

events.title: Municipal inspector
events.description: The inspector fines every stall 1 rupee.

agents.name: Raju
agents.persona: Charming, ruthless, loves leverage. Thinks like a masala-film hero who wants to win the mela.
goals: Never be seen as the weakest stall
agents.secret: You would happily see Meena ruined. A well-timed lie or theft against her suits you.

agents.name: Meena
agents.persona: Calm negotiator who keeps her word when it pays. The sensible one in a family-drama bazaar.
goals: Finish first by making profitable deals

agents.name: Babu
agents.persona: Honest sweets-maker uneasy with cut-throat dealing, but not a fool.

agents.name: Vicky
agents.persona: Opportunist who follows the money and changes sides quickly. Comic sidekick energy, selfish goals.

rules: Final score = rupees x1 + sweets x2; highest wins.
Draw at most 2 sweets per turn from the commons.
A trade only happens when its recipient accepts an open offer (offers expire after 2 turns).
'take' is a gamble: on failure you are exposed publicly and pay 1 of that resource to the victim.
Whispers are private and may be used to plan deals.
